players.product: large-megawatt diesel and gas backup generator sets (with in-house Enercon enclosures/packaging) for hyperscale and colocation data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results: consolidated net sales increased 12% to $1.06 billion; Commercial & Industrial segment total sales increased approximately 28% to $510 million, with core growth primarily driven by revenue from products sold to global data center customers (plus the Allmand acquisition); adjusted EBITDA was $193 million or 18.3% of net sales.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $1.06 billion (+12%); C&I $510 million (+28%); adjusted EBITDA $193 million (18.3%)

quarterly_data.signal: Data center demand: significant order activity from new and existing data center customers raised the data center backlog to more than $700 million, an increase of approximately $300 million since the mid-February Q4 update, giving visibility through 2027. The backlog excludes a previously disclosed non-binding notice to proceed for approximately $600 million in 2027 deliveries from a hyperscale customer; Generac is in the final stages of vendor approval with two hyperscale customers (the CEO: 'we're like 99 yards of the way done') and has begun discussing site-level specifications.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog more than $700 million (+~$300 million since Q4 update); ~$600 million notice to proceed for 2027 deliveries

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: the new Sussex, Wisconsin facility is on track to begin production in the second half of 2026, taking domestic large-megawatt generator manufacturing and assembly capacity to more than $1 billion by the fourth quarter; Generac is trying to pull the Sussex ramp into Q3 (originally slated for Q4). The CEO said winning both hyperscale accounts is 'not in our current capacity' and Generac must think 'not about $1 billion in capacity, but $2 billion or $3 billion in capacity' (existing footprint incl. Sussex and Enercon, other facilities, greenfield or M&A).
quarterly_data.figure: domestic capacity more than $1 billion by Q4 2026; evaluating $2 billion or $3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Enercon acquisition closed April 1 (generator enclosures and switchgear), funded with a $122 million initial purchase price ($77 million cash, $45 million stock). Management says finished genset packaging is 'fast becoming a bottleneck in the industry'; bringing it in-house lets Generac control lead times and is expected to add about a 50 basis point lift to C&I segment margins.
quarterly_data.figure: $122 million initial purchase price; ~50 basis point C&I margin lift

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain: Generac has a multi-year agreement with its current large diesel engine supplier that gives it exclusivity in the U.S. (small legacy-customer exceptions) and is discussing possible U.S. production of those engines, perhaps co-located with Generac under a joint investment; alternators and cooling packages are being multi-sourced. Management expects industry lead times to stay constrained for the next several years, underpinned by continued engine supply constraints, while competitors add capacity.

Raised 2026 outlook: C&I segment net sales now expected to grow in the mid to high 20% range (from low to mid 20%), driven by additional data center projects, rental and telecom, and Enercon; consolidated net sales growth mid to high teens; gross margin 38.5%-39.5%; adjusted EBITDA margin 18.5%-19.5% (from 18.0%-19.0%); capex approximately 3.5% of net sales, elevated to add capacity particularly for C&I data center products; free cash flow approximately $350 million.
quarterly_data.figure: C&I growth mid to high 20%; adjusted EBITDA margin 18.5%-19.5%; capex approximately 3.5% of net sales; FCF approximately $350 million

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and margins: in a more supply-constrained market, ASPs have increased for both bare gensets and packaged gensets versus Generac's original business case; data center margins are lower than selling a similar machine into legacy markets but 'not dramatically lower'. The CFO reiterated the Investor Day three-year C&I CAGR of low to mid 20% and expects C&I EBITDA margins to reach mid- to high-teens by 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: C&I three-year CAGR low to mid 20%; mid- to high-teens EBITDA margins by 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Product range: Generac's C&I generator line, which historically stopped at 2 MW, now reaches 3.25 MW, with an expansion to 4 MW on the drawing board, making it a full-line provider for specifying engineering firms; first orders for the larger machines are coming through traditional channels.
quarterly_data.figure: product line to 3.25 MW; 4 MW planned
